lines.trans: I believe there is a problem with the prevailing attitude in Japan.
Japan has a culture of modesty.
There is no need to be bound by it.
But I don't think it's embarrassing at all.
Living as you truly are is what makes us human.
My theme is love.
And love is the acceptance of nature.
Thank you very much.
I will show you all the moment a miracle happens.
Please do not close your eyes.
Ready? Here we go, then.
Ready, action!

meanings.note: Standalone casual thanks; followed by ございます (present) or ございました (completed occasion) for polite thanks.

examples.text: ありがとうございます。

meanings.en: exist; be available; remain in place
meanings.note: Used for inanimate things and abstract concepts; after て-form (書いてある, 置いてある) describes a resulting state left in place.

examples.text: 名前が書いてあります。

meanings.en: as it is; one's natural, unaltered state
meanings.note: Often used with に (あるがままに) to mean 'just as one is'.

examples.text: あるがままを受け入れる。

meanings.note: Irregular i-adjective whose past/conditional stems use よ- (よかったら).

examples.text: よかったら来てください。

meanings.note: Prefixed to native Japanese words (お店, お二人, お持ち帰り) to add politeness.
Humble counterpart of いる, commonly used in ～ております.
Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.note: Follows a verb's て-form or polite お + stem (お待ちください, お持ち帰りください) to make a polite request.

examples.text: ここに書いてください。

meanings.note: Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。

meanings.en: polite auxiliary in ありがとうございます
meanings.note: Survives in modern speech chiefly in ございます (present) and ございました (past) after ありがとう and おめでとう.

examples.text: ありがとうございます。
ありがとうございました。
examples.trans: Thank you very much (for what just concluded).

meanings.note: All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
Connects clauses or sentences.

examples.trans: I studied, and then went to sleep.

examples.text: そして次の日になった。
examples.trans: And then the next day came.

meanings.note: In casual speech, それ plus は often fuses into そりゃ ('well, as for that / of course').
Formal/polite transition; contracts to それじゃ or じゃあ in casual speech.

examples.text: それでは始めましょう。

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

meanings.note: Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.en: whichever (after question word); or something like
meanings.note: After どれ (どれでも) means 'any one at all'; after a noun (店でも) suggests an example ('a shop or something').

examples.text: いつでも来てください。
お茶でも飲みませんか。
examples.trans: Won't you have tea or something?

meanings.note: Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.
Colloquial quotative/emphatic particle expressing surprise or dismissal.

examples.text: そんなことなんて知らない。
examples.trans: I don't know anything like that.

examples.text: 嘘だなんて信じられない。
examples.trans: I can't believe it's a lie.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Cue word used before starting a race or filming.
Attaches to the irrealis (a-stem) of godan verbs.

examples.trans: I was called by the teacher.

meanings.note: Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.
Polite/dialectal negative ending, especially in ～ません.
Film/theater cue or general noun from English 'action'.

examples.text: 次のアクションを起こす。

meanings.note: Loanword from German 'Thema'.

examples.text: 今日のテーマは愛です。
新しいテーマを決める。

meanings.note: Loanword from English 'miracle'.
Formed from 人間らしい ('human-like') + -さ.

examples.text: 人間らしさを大切にする。
そこに人間らしさがある。

meanings.note: Polite volitional 会いましょう in また会いましょう means 'let us meet again'.

examples.trans: I meet a friend at the station.

examples.text: また来週会いましょう。

meanings.note: Humble counterpart of 行く and 来る.

examples.text: それでは参りましょう。

meanings.note: Formal noun.

examples.text: 新しい考えを受容する。

meanings.note: Used for social/work issues as well as test questions.

examples.text: それは大きな問題です。
特に問題はありません。

meanings.note: Used with が before it (ストーリーが必要だ 'a story is needed') or な before a noun.

meanings.en: to think; to feel; to believe
meanings.note: Often follows quotative と to express an opinion or belief.

examples.text: それはいいと思います。

meanings.note: Derived from the verb 恥じる (to feel shy/ashamed).

examples.text: 彼女には恥じらいがある。
examples.trans: She has a sense of modesty.

meanings.note: i-adjective describing embarrassment or self-consciousness.

examples.text: ちょっと恥ずかしいです。
恥ずかしい思いをした。

meanings.note: Noun.
Refers to the customs, arts, and social institutions of a group.
Read にほん (Nihon) or にっぽん (Nippon).

examples.text: 日本の文化が好きです。

meanings.note: Ichidan verb.
Polite way to address a group of people.

examples.text: 皆さんにお知らせがあります。
examples.trans: I have an announcement for everyone.

meanings.note: Noun.
Noun.

examples.text: その瞬間を待っていた。
examples.trans: I was waiting for that moment.

meanings.note: Standard gender-neutral 'I' in polite and business Japanese.

meanings.en: to tie; to bind; to restrict
meanings.note: Often used figuratively in the passive 縛られる ('to be bound by').

examples.text: ルールに縛られたくない。
examples.trans: I don't want to be bound by rules.
Tie up the luggage with string.

meanings.note: Can also function as a na-adjective meaning 'natural'.

meanings.en: to happen; to occur; to wake up
meanings.note: Ichidan verb.

examples.trans: I wake up at seven every morning.

meanings.note: Ichidan verb, used for eyes, books, doors, etc.

meanings.en: social trend; prevailing attitude or climate
meanings.note: Refers to the general mood or tendency in society.

examples.text: 最近の風潮が変わってきた。
examples.trans: Recent social trends have started to change.

examples.text: そういう風潮に流されたくない。
examples.trans: I don't want to be swept up in that kind of trend.
